module_title: Group-wise Trends, Hydration, and Boron/Carbon Families (Intermediate)
introduction: This level drives into group-specific chemistry, mapping out solubility and thermal stability trends for s-block salts. It also covers the core properties of the Boron (Group 13) and Carbon (Group 14) families, emphasizing specific industrial compounds and structural allotropes.

core_concepts.title: Hydration Enthalpy vs. Lattice Enthalpy Trends
core_concepts.description: Hydration enthalpy is inversely proportional to ionic size ($1/r$). For alkali metals, the trend is: $Li^+ > Na^+ > K^+ > Rb^+ > Cs^+$. Because $Li^+$ has the highest hydration enthalpy, it exists heavily hydrated in solution, making hydrated $Li^+$ the largest ion in size and giving it the lowest ionic mobility (conductivity) in water.

core_concepts.title: Solubility and Thermal Stability of s-Block Salts
core_concepts.description:
1. Thermal Stability: Carbonates and sulfates of Group 1 and 2 become MORE stable down the group because the larger cation stabilizes the larger polyatomic anion through better lattice packing (e.g., $BaCO_3 > CaCO_3$).
2. Solubility: For sulfates and hydroxides of Group 2, lattice enthalpy remains nearly constant down the group, but hydration enthalpy drops rapidly. Thus, Sulfates become LESS soluble down the group ($MgSO_4$ is highly soluble, $BaSO_4$ is insoluble). Hydroxides become MORE soluble down the group.

core_concepts.title: Group 13: Boron Family and Diborane Structure
core_concepts.description:
Boron forms electron-deficient compounds due to having only 3 valence electrons. The most critical compound is Diborane ($B_2H_6$). It cannot be explained by standard covalent bonding. 
Structure: It contains two terminal B-H bonds per boron atom (normal 2-centre-2-electron bonds) and two bridging B-H-B bonds. These bridging bonds are unique **3-centre-2-electron bonds** (also known as banana bonds), where an electron pair is shared across three atomic centers.

core_concepts.title: Group 14: Carbon Family and Allotropes
core_concepts.description:
Carbon exhibits catenation (the ability to form long chains) due to its high C-C bond energy. 
Allotropes:
1. Diamond: $sp^3$ hybridized, continuous 3D tetrahedral network. Crystalline, hardest natural substance, electrical insulator.
2. Graphite: $sp^2$ hybridized, planar hexagonal layers held by weak van der Waals forces. Each C atom has one free unhybridized electron, making it an excellent electrical conductor.
3. Fullerenes ($C_{60}$): Cage-like buckyball molecules containing both five-membered and six-membered rings.

important_entities.name: Borax and Inorganic Benzene
important_entities.significance: Borazine is structurally completely isoelectronic and isosteric to benzene, sharing a similar planar ring with alternating B and N atoms. It is prepared by reacting diborane with ammonia: $3B_2H_6 + 6NH_3 \rightarrow 2B_3N_3H_6 + 12H_2$.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A high-frequency NEET/JEE question: Moving down Group 13, you expect radius to increase monotonically. However, the atomic radius of Gallium (Ga) is smaller than Aluminum (Al) ($r_{\text{Ga}} < r_{\text{Al}}$). This exception happens because Gallium is preceded by ten 3d transition elements. The 3d electrons offer extremely poor shielding, causing a sharp increase in $Z_{\text{eff}}$ that pulls the valence shell inward.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the solubility trends of Alkaline Earth Metal ($M^{2+}$) salts down the group: **Sulfates** decrease in solubility down the group (they sink to the bottom as precipitates like $BaSO_4$), while **Hydroxides** increase in solubility down the group ($Ba(OH)_2$ is highly soluble).

exam_strategy_tips: In Borax Bead test problems, remember that Borax ($Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O$) when heated loses water and swells, eventually forming a transparent glassy bead containing sodium metaborate ($NaBO_2$) and boric anhydride ($B_2O_3$). This bead reacts with transition metal oxides to form characteristically colored metaborate beads (e.g., $Cu^{2+}$ gives a blue bead).
